newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler says Bavarian CPI data not surprising.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler says Bavarian CPI data not surprising.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Friday that the slight acceleration in Bavarian consumer price inflation in January was not surprising.
Bavarian CPI rose 1.6 percent year-on-year in January, a slight increase from 1.4 percent in December.

Zeitler said the Bavarian rise was more or less in line with a country-wide trend. He also said the rise in prices was due to several one-off reasons, including an increase in television and radio usage fees.
Zeitler also said that the Bavarian data did not reflect any impact of higher import prices, although this aspect should be kept under observation.
His comments were released in a statement.
